chapter: Young players, schools and studio work
title: Requirements of a studio musician
summary: Reading, tone, patience, controlling your ego and reliability on dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Just for posterity and for young people that would be listening, knowing you're a great player and you're not only a man that plays first, but you've been also a jazz player and have been known for that, doing that, and still doing it. Can you just sort of cite for young people some of the requirements of a studio musician?

Well, the first requirement is that you have to be an awfully good reader, you know, and don't make too many mistakes. Even when they write the mistakes, you have to have a good enough ear not to play the mistakes. Some guys like to make a big fuss, say, I've got a mistake in bar such and such. And he knows damn well what the right note is but he just wants to let the arranger know he's on the ball. But actually what he's doing, he's taking up valuable time, he's a pain in the neck. Most good studio players, they find a wrong note; they correct it. You know, if you know it's wrong then you know what the right one should be. And any guy who says, I've got a wrong note, it's only because he wants to attract attention.
I know, I did it myself until I realized I didn't have

to do that kind of corny stuff. But that's the first requirement. And of course, naturally with that goes you have to have pretty good command of your instrument. That means you have to be able to play a tune, you have to be a good reader, you have to play in tune, you have to have a fairly good tone, whatever the standards of a good tone are. I think there are absolute standards but there are also popular standards and you have to come under that category.

If you've got a good tone by traditional standards, you can work in almost any kind of job. And if you're sort of a specialized tone, then you're going to be in specialized kind of work and you won't do all the work. So the more you have going for you, the more work you can do.

And you have to be able to get along with people. You have to be able to control your own ego. You can come in on a date and think you're the greatest first trumpet player in the world and you see the worst first trumpet player in the world, in your opinion, is playing first because that's who the leader wanted, you've got to be able to sit there and cooperate and not make a big scene out of it. And even if you don't enjoy it, you've got to at least act like you enjoy it because if you make waves, they're not going to hire you. It's just a very simple thing. You know, honey attracts more flies than vinegar. So if you want to work, you have to learn to be patient, you have to learn to sit for a long time while they

seem to do meaningless things, you have to put up with what you think is an injustice, that means you didn't get to play parts that you thought you should have gotten to play. And in general, you just have to behave like an adult, as much as possible.

And, of course, it goes without saying that you have to be a reliable person. You have to show up on time, you have to -- don't show up drunk or get drunk when you're on the date, make a lot of noise. There have been guys pass a bottle around or try smoking dope, but they don't last long.

They think they're going to change the whole world, like they've just discovered dope or whiskey or something. And you know, the older guys are sitting there thinking how they outgrew that a long time ago, it's time you outgrew it.
